subject: Post-call: Pen test & retention requirements — action items and owners
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira@acrobank.com>, Mike Li <mike.li@acrobank.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 10 Aug 2026 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: Pen test & retention requirements — action items and owners

Hi Samira / Mike,

Thanks again for the time today — helpful conversation. Putting the recap, the explicit asks you raised, and proposed owners/timelines below so we have a clear next step plan.

Summary of pain points you shared
- Audit log retention: 7 years for transaction and admin logs, searchable by transaction ID and account ID.
- Pen test evidence: need test reports + remediation confirmation for infra and our public API endpoints.
- SOC 2: you require current Type II report or a plan + timeline to obtain Type II within procurement window.
- DPA & data residency: standard DPA with clause to keep production data in us-east-1; proof of in-region backups.
- Short data exposure window requirement for debug logs (max 30 days unless requested).

What Redwood can provide (high level)
- SOC 2: we are SOC 2 in progress; we can share the Type II report once available (ETA Q4 2026) and provide our interim SOC 2 bridge documents and control matrix now. (Attachment: redwood-soc2-summary.pdf)
- Pen test: we can share the most recent third-party test report and an artifact list to demonstrate remediation steps. We suggest a targeted re-test scoped to your external-facing app endpoints. (Attachment: pen-test-ask-list.xlsx)
- Audit logs & retention: we expose immutable audit logs via API and can configure retention policies per account; can provide a sample retention policy and an extract of schema + example queries.
- DPA: redwood standard DPA supports region scoping and KMS-based key control; legal can produce an addendum for in-region backups.

Action items & owners (proposed)
1) Jordan: Share SOC 2 interim artifacts, control matrix, and SOC timeline — by Wed 2026-08-12 EOD.
2) Karthik: Share pen-test report and the remediation tracker + propose scope for AcroBank-focused retest — by Fri 2026-08-14.
3) Lauren: Draft DPA addendum language for in-region backups + retention SLAs and circulate to your legal — by Tue 2026-08-18.
4) Samira / Mike: Confirm whether AcroBank legal needs any additional clauses beyond in-region backups and a 7-year audit log retention requirement — by Fri 2026-08-14.

Please flag any corrections to the above. If that looks right, I’ll also open a HubSpot task for each action item and loop in our security engineering lead for the pen test scope call.

Thanks — Jordan

--
Jordan Blake
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
(j) 415-555-0142
https://redwood.com
From: Samira Khan <samira@acrobank.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Mike Li <mike.li@acrobank.com>
Date: Mon, 10 Aug 2026 16:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: Pen test & retention requirements — action items and owners

Jordan — thanks for the tidy recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

- SOC 2: AcroBank needs either an active Type II (preferred) or a signed commitment with milestones and compensating controls. Q4 is acceptable if there are concrete milestone dates and a contact in security we can rely on.
- Pen test: We will want the pen-test scope to include both API endpoints and any web-facing console. We also need evidence of remediation (tickets + verification) for any medium/high findings in the last 12 months.
- Audit logs: the 7-year retention is non-negotiable for transaction logs; admin logs can be 2 years. Queryability by transaction ID is critical.
- Data residency: in-region backups are mandatory; encryption keys must be KMS-managed within us-east-1.

We can confirm our legal requirements by Friday 2026-08-14. In terms of next steps, please send the SOC interim artifacts and the pen-test report so our security team can triage. Also, can you confirm the format of the audit log export (JSON vs CSV) and whether we can pull via API?

Samira

--
Samira Khan
Head of Vendor Risk | AcroBank
samira@acrobank.com
+1 212-555-0199
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Samira Khan <samira@acrobank.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Mike Li <mike.li@acrobank.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 10 Aug 2026 18:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: Pen test & retention requirements — action items and owners

Hi Samira — looping in with the pen test artifacts. Attaching the latest third-party report and a remediation tracker in the XLSX (see attached list in the HubSpot link; sending redwood-soc2-summary.pdf to Jordan to append).

Quick answers to Samira's format questions:
- Audit log export: we support both JSON and CSV exports. Production-grade API access is available for accounts with dedicated keys; we can provide sample cURLs and a short script to pull logs by transaction ID.
- API access: yes, customer-side API keys, scoped to read-only audit endpoints.

Proposed immediate next step: 30-minute technical scope call between our security engineering lead (I’ll add them once Jordan okays) and your security engineer to align on pen test boundaries and success criteria. Available windows: Thu 2026-08-13 10:00-12:00 PT or Fri 2026-08-14 14:00-16:00 PT. Which works for you?

Thanks,
Karthik

--
Karthik Iyer
Director, Security Solutions | Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.com
From: Mike Li <mike.li@acrobank.com>

Date: Tue, 11 Aug 2026 09:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: Pen test & retention requirements — action items and owners

Thanks all — Thu 2026-08-13 10:30 PT works for our security engineer. We also confirm JSON export preference for audit logs; CSV is ok as fallback.

We’ll circulate our legal must-haves by EOD Fri 2026-08-14. For planning, please assume we will request a copy of the final SOC 2 Type II report as a condition of contracting.

Regards,
Mike
